first_impression.reaction: It answers the question in the first two sentences, no fluff, no sales pitch. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, and the answers are short and match the body. It's a how-to on wording, not something I'd usually hold a planner to, but nothing here is trying to sell me before it's helped me. I'll skim the rest.

journey.quote: Send a gentle reminder before your reply date, a personal follow-up once it has passed, and a last call only if a name is still blank.
journey.reaction: Straight answer up top. Good. That's the whole process in one line and I can stop there if I want.

journey.quote: Time every reminder from your own reply date and the date your venue and caterer need final numbers, not from a fixed rule.
journey.reaction: Part of me wants a number of days. But I'd rather they admit it depends on the caterer than make one up that every other site copies. Fair.

journey.section: Who to remind and how to reach them
journey.quote: As general information as at November 2026, not legal advice: the Privacy Act does not cover individuals acting in a personal capacity, and in some situations state or territory laws may also apply.
journey.reaction: Dated, sourced to the OAIC, and honest that it's not legal advice. That's the kind of line I actually check, and it holds up.

journey.section: Who to remind and how to reach them
journey.quote: If your guest list spans several countries and a weekend of events, talk to Wedded Concierge about planning the celebration around it.
journey.reaction: First pitch turns up before I've even seen a single piece of the wording I came for. It's short and it's relevant to destination weddings, so it's not a big deal, but it reads as a bit early.

journey.section: RSVP reminder cards for a formal invitation suite
journey.quote: Scammers can use QR codes to hide harmful links, and a guest cannot check where a QR code leads before scanning it.
journey.reaction: Practical and sourced to the government cyber site. Didn't expect that in a wording article. Useful.

journey.section: Reminding guests for a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone.
journey.reaction: Clear enough on scope. 'Payments' is the word that makes me ask the obvious: if the Advisor handles payments to vendors, do they take a cut along the way? The page doesn't say.

journey.section: Deciding whether to count a guest
journey.quote: Counting a quiet guest as attending is the cautious choice for catering; counting them as declined protects a tight venue capacity.
journey.reaction: An actual trade-off, laid out both ways. This is the bit I'd show my fiancee.

journey.section: Keep one list so you only remind the right guests
journey.quote: Nothing sours goodwill faster than reminding someone who has already answered.
journey.reaction: 'Nothing ... faster' is a superlative nobody can back up. The point is fine, the phrasing is marketing.

journey.section: Keep one list so you only remind the right guests
journey.quote: Wonderland Studio, our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, keeps that list in one place.
journey.reaction: OK, is the app free, or is it part of a package? First thing I'd want to know before I put my guest list in it.

journey.section: Ready to plan the weekend around the replies
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Confirms inclusions in writing before you commit' is the most reassuring thing on the page for someone who's been burned before. Concrete. Still no fee model though.

journey.section: Ready to plan the weekend around the replies
journey.quote: Once the replies are in, the real planning begins: where everyone stays, how each event runs and who pays whom, and when.
journey.reaction: 'The real planning begins' is a bit of a brochure line. The rest of the sentence is concrete, so it's only the opener.

unanswered_questions: How is a Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage, or commission from venues and suppliers?
When the Advisor plans 'payments', does money pass through Wedded Wonderland, and is there any mark-up on supplier prices?
Is Wonderland Studio free to use, or only included with a paid planning service?
Where is my guest list data stored if I use Wonderland Studio, and who can see it?

turn_offs_found.quote: Nothing sours goodwill faster than reminding someone who has already answered.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported superlative in an article that otherwise sticks to plain advice and sources.

turn_offs_found.quote: If your guest list spans several countries and a weekend of events, talk to Wedded Concierge about planning the celebration around it.
turn_offs_found.why: First CTA lands before any of the wording the page promised. Mild, because it is short and on topic.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the last call wording and the 'count them or not' trade-off
My mum, who'll be chasing her side of the family anyway

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The closing CTA comes after real help and promises inclusions in writing, which is what I want. I'd click only to find the fee model and whether there are supplier commissions. If the Concierge page doesn't answer that, I'm not enquiring.
